about: How a house rule is named, in every namespace and both languages: <category>-<verb>-<object> after the namespace, with the category and the verb from these closed lists. Ported rules keep their upstream names and are not judged here. Adding a category or a verb is a decision about the scheme, so it is made here, once, and both engines read it.

verbs.name: require
verbs.definition: The construct must appear, or take this shape.

categories.name: boundary
categories.definition: Which module, library or layer may reach into which.

categories.name: concurrency
categories.definition: Work that interleaves: races, suspension points, isolation escapes.

categories.name: consistency
categories.definition: One house spelling for names, comments, folders and syntax, where two forms would work.

categories.name: correctness
categories.definition: Code that compiles but doesn't do what it reads as doing.

categories.name: import
categories.definition: How an import is written: alias, namespace, source.

categories.name: network
categories.definition: Structure's NetworkService is the only door to the network and its cache.

categories.name: next
categories.definition: Next.js App Router file and export conventions.

categories.name: performance
categories.definition: Cost the code pays for nothing.

categories.name: react-component
categories.definition: How a React component is declared, named, typed and exported.

categories.name: react-element
categories.definition: JSX elements that have a house component instead.

categories.name: react-hook
categories.definition: How hooks are called, named and given dependencies.

categories.name: security
categories.definition: Untrusted values reaching a shell, SQL, or other interpreter.

categories.name: storage
categories.definition: Browser storage goes through its service.

categories.name: toolchain
categories.definition: Compiler, language mode and package settings every target must carry.

namespaces.name: adamic
namespaces.definition: The soundness holes tsc leaves open and Adamic closes. Each name is Adamic's own, from adamic docs/0.1.md, so one rule has one name in both projects; the list is closed, and a name joins it there first.

names.name: invariant-mutable
names.definition: A mutable location (an element, a mutable property, a map value) is not seen through a wider type.

names.name: no-definite-assignment
names.definition: No definite assignment assertion, `field!: T`, which reads undefined as T.

names.name: no-optional-widening
names.definition: A value is not seen as a type with an optional property its own type does not declare.

names.name: no-type-predicate
names.definition: No written type predicate, which the checker trusts and never verifies.

names.name: no-unchecked-cast
names.definition: No cast the runtime cannot check; an upcast and a checked downcast to a union member are allowed.

names.name: nominal-class
names.definition: A class type accepts only instances of that class, with identical type arguments.

names.name: single-spread
names.definition: An object literal spreads at most once, as its first member.
